conviction_note: Event confirmed by the company's own 2026-10-05 release (Q2 FY27 results 2026-10-19 after 16:00 ET, webinar 2026-10-20 08:00 ET). Arithmetic from the Q1 FY27 SENS plus the Q2 FY26 base points to a quarter roughly in line to slightly above a ~$0.57-0.59 EPS / $98.8M revenue bar, with mild positives (SA vehicle demand, peer Samsara's strong print, Q1 gross margin above the guided range) offset by the CEO's own statement that the next three quarters focus on cross-selling rather than greenfield adds, which makes a step-down from the record 142,472 Q1 net adds likely. That nets to a small positive lean (p_up 53). The real print-reaction history, rebuilt from confirmed releases because the baseline's is 6-K noise, is large and two-sided (-16.5%, ~+8%, -6%, +11%), so abs_move is 9 and the scaled number is small; impact_sum (+1.3) is larger than the scaled number because the findings are individually small leans that each lack decisive evidence.

findings.finding: Arithmetic from primary documents: Q2 FY26 Karooooo subscription revenue was ZAR1,182m (Cartrack ZAR1,180m) and Q1 FY27 grew 19% reported / 21% constant currency to ZAR1,354m; repeating ~19-20% on the Q2 base gives ~ZAR1,410-1,420m subscription revenue and ~ZAR1.62-1.64bn total revenue (Q1: ZAR1.56bn incl. DaaS ZAR177m), which at the ~R16.0-16.4/USD that prevailed June-August 2026 (vs ~R16.2 at Q1's May 31 translation) is ~$99-101M against the $98.8M consensus, i.e. a ~1% USD revenue beat if Q1's growth rate merely holds; adjusted EPS at +18-21% on Q2 FY26's ZAR8.28 is ZAR9.8-10.0, ~$0.60-0.61 vs $0.57-0.59.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 (2025-10-14): revenue +21% and slight USD revenue beat but EPS 'miss' ($0.44 vs $0.46 per Benzinga) and S&M +34% -> stock -16.5% on the day (https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/10/15/why-karooooo-limited-plunged-today). Q1 FY27 (2026-07-15): EPS $0.59 vs $0.51 plus record adds -> +11.2% (baseline amc row). The stock trades on margins/adds more than on the revenue line.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus is a USD number built on an FX assumption nobody publishes; the rand held ~R16.0-16.4 through June-August (valutafx, https://www.valutafx.com/history/usd-zar-2026-08-21 : 16.019 on 2026-08-21; https://www.valutafx.com/history/usd-zar-2026-07-07 : 16.317), which is slightly kinder to USD-translated numbers than Q1. But this sits inside the company's own 18-24% guide, so it is largely expected; if the market priced a clear beat the stock would not be 5% down over 20 days with consensus EPS only flat vs Q1's $0.59.
findings.independence: Q2 FY26 base from the company's 2025-10-14 release (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251014185729/en/Karooooo-Accelerates-Subscription-Revenue-Growth-from-15-to-20); FX from valutafx. All arithmetic is mine, not a company number.

findings.finding: On the Q1 FY27 call (2026-07-16) CEO Zak Calisto said 'we are going to focus probably the next three quarters more on cross-selling to our base' after pursuing greenfield in Q1, declined subscriber guidance, and said Cartrack-Tag (a material driver of the record 142,472 Q1 net adds, SA +92% to 113,913) carries much lower ARPU than average; with Q2 FY26 net adds having already fallen q/q (H1 FY26 154,753 minus Q1 84,013 = ~70,740), Q2 FY27 net adds are likely to step down from the Q1 record, a headline the market rewarded with +11% last time.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Record net adds were the headline of the Q1 FY27 release and the stock rose 11.2% (https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260715045842/en/Karooooo-Reports-Q1-2027-Results-with-Record-Net-Subscriber-Additions-and-Accelerating-Growth); Q3 FY26 'record subscriber growth' was bought ~+8% (https://www-web.itiger.com/news/1169627692).
findings.why_not_priced: It was said on a public call, so the covering analysts heard it; but the stock ran to its 52w high (~$68.80) after a release headlined 'record net subscriber additions and accelerating growth', and the 20-day drift lower is small. If the market fully expected a sharp step-down in adds, the multiple built on the Q1 record would already have compressed further. Partly priced, hence small.
findings.independence: Q2 FY26 net adds derived from the company's own H1 FY26 figure (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/35443426/karooooo-accelerates-subscription-revenue-growth-from-15-to-20). Transcript is a third-party transcription with some name errors.

findings.finding: South African new-vehicle demand stayed strong through the quarter (June 2026 the highest June total in 19 years; August 2026 total sales 57,898, +11.4% y/y, light commercials +11% to 13,727, medium commercial +16.3%, heavy +10.1%), supporting Cartrack's South African subscriber funnel, which supplied ~80% of Q1 net adds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history; subscriber adds are a line this stock has reacted to (+11% on the Q1 record).
findings.why_not_priced: Macro proxy that US holders of a Nasdaq listing rarely map to Cartrack; but most Cartrack subscribers attach to the installed fleet, not to new-vehicle sales, so transmission is weak.
findings.independence: June 2026 record: https://www.timeslive.co.za/motoring/2026-07-01-south-africas-new-vehicle-sales-hit-highest-june-total-in-19-years/ . Proxy only; partly offset by the CEO's cross-sell comment (finding 2), which concerns the company's sales focus rather than market demand.

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 subscription gross margin was 73%, above the 70-72% FY27 guide, and operating margin 28% sat inside 27-30%; management kept the range only as 'prudent', expects S&M growth to slow vs FY26 and a hiring slowdown, so the half-year print is a natural point to firm or lift the margin/EPS guide (FY EPS ZAR38.50-40.00 needs ~ZAR9.7-10.2 a quarter after Q1's 9.53).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (Jan 2026) raised outlook midpoint -> ~+8%; FY26 results with a contracting gross-margin outlook for FY27 (May 2026) -> -6.07% (baseline amc row 2026-05-13); Q2 FY26 margin pressure -> -16.5%. Margin and guide direction are the lines this stock moves on.
findings.why_not_priced: Guidance was left unchanged in July despite the 73% margin, and the consensus EPS for Q2 ($0.57-0.59) is no higher than Q1's actual $0.59, so the Street is not modelling margin upside. If a raise were priced the stock would be at or above its post-Q1 high rather than 10% below it.
findings.independence: Guide figures from the Q1 SENS PDF (https://karooooo.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/KARO-Q1FY2027-SENS-20260716.pdf), same company source family as finding 1 but a different line (guidance vs reported quarter).

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 free cash flow collapsed to ZAR60m (from ZAR338m) because the company pre-bought IoT devices held for future use (+ZAR163m to ZAR524m) and IoT prepayments (+ZAR53m); with that inventory already on the balance sheet, Q2 device capex for future use should be lower and FCF should recover, which management said the Q1 decline 'does not indicate a structural issue'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history on FCF alone; the Q1 FCF drop did not stop a +11% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference; if accelerated adds continue, device investment stays high and FCF may stay weak, so this is a small two-sided lean.
findings.independence: CFO comment on the call (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2939731). Shares the SENS PDF with findings 1 and 4 but on a separate line.

findings.finding: Peer Samsara reported its quarter to 2026-08-01 on 2026-09-03, after Karooooo last spoke: revenue $508.4M +30%, ARR $2.125bn +30%, adjusted EPS $0.20 vs $0.16, raised full-year guide, stock +13% after hours; connected-operations demand through the same months as Karooooo's Q2 was strong.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured for KARO on peer prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Different customer base (US enterprise vs SA SMB fleets), so transmission is weak; KARO fell ~5% over the last 20 days, so the peer read has not lifted it.
